items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve portions of a Maryland state implementation plan (SIP) submission as adequate to meet certain Clean Air Act (CAA) interstate transport requirements for the 2010 primary sulfur dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) national ambient air quality standard (NAAQS). Specifically, the EPA proposes to find that the SIP submission demonstrates that the Maryland SIP contains adequate provisions prohibiting emissions from Maryland sources from contributing significantly to nonattainment or interfering with maintenance of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS in any other state. This action is being taken under the CAA.

This SIP (or "attainment plan") includes Texas' attainment demonstration provisions and emissions inventory for the nonattainment area, demonstration of reasonable further progress (RFP), implementation of reasonably available control measures (RACM) (including reasonably available control technology (RACT)), an approved nonattainment new source review (NNSR) program,…
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Texas; Attainment Plan for the Navarro County 2010 Sulfur Dioxide Primary National Ambient Air Quality Standard Nonattainment Area

items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve State Implementation Plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of Utah on February 28, 2025. The Utah submittal includes revisions to the State's Administrative Rule R307-110-36, concerning SIP Section X Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance (I/M) Program, Part F, Cache County. These revisions updated the rule effectiveness date, updated the definition of vehicle I/M program stations, added emergency vehicle exemptions, and added a part unavailability waiver to the Cache County, Utah I/M program.
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Utah; Cache County Inspection and Maintenance Program Revision

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a state implementation plan (SIP) revision (Revision A25) submitted by the Commonwealth of Virginia. This revision pertains to an amendment made in the Virginia Administrative Code (VAC) to include minor New Source Review (NSR) permit exemptions for bovine incinerators for agricultural use. This action is being taken under the Clean Air Act (CAA).
items.title: Air Plan Approval; Virginia; Revision to Minor New Source Review Permit Exemptions

items.summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to conditionally approve a revision to the San Diego County Air Pollution Control District (SDCAPCD or "District") portion of the California State implementation plan (SIP). This revision concerns emissions of oxides of nitrogen (NO<INF>X</INF>) from landfill flares. We are conditionally approving a local rule to regulate these emission sources under the Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act").

items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Region 9 is proposing to reissue an NPDES general permit for water discharges from bulk fuel facilities located in Guam (Permit No. GUG000001). The permit will be reissued upon completion of the notice and comment period and after due consideration has been given to all comments received. items.summary: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC, Commission, or Agency) proposes to establish a new system of records, FCC/OEA-7, Foreign Adversary Risk Management System (FARMS), subject to the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended. This action is necessary to meet the requirements of the Privacy Act to publish in the Federal Register notice of the creation, existence, and character of records maintained by the Agency. The Commission uses this system to collect information on whether FCC regulatees are subject to the control or other influence of a foreign adversary or adversarial country, as well as ownership and other information on the nature of any regulatees subject to adversarial control.

items.summary: EPA is proposing to revise the regulations defining solid wastes that are not hazardous wastes by adding a new exclusion. The proposed revision specifies that leather articles used as personal protective equipment are not hazardous wastes when discarded, if they meet the same standards applicable to the currently excluded waste scrap leather from various leather product manufacturing industries.
items.title: Reducing Complexity in Management of Leather Waste
